categories.name: Synthesizers
categories.blurb: Polyphonic Voice Cells for chords and keys: patch Notes in and Out L/R out.

categories.name: Basses
categories.blurb: Monophonic and duophonic Voice Cells for bass lines, from sub and acid to reese, FM and wobble: patch Notes in and Out L/R out.

categories.name: Leads
categories.blurb: Monophonic and few-voice Voice Cells for melodies and solos, from vintage saws to sync, FM, vocal and chip leads: patch Notes in and Out L/R out.

categories.name: Pads
categories.blurb: Slow, wide, moving Voice Cells for chords, beds and drones: patch Notes in and Out L/R out.

categories.name: Plucks & Mallets
categories.blurb: Struck, plucked and pinged Voice Cells (physical models, mallets, strings and bells) that follow velocity: patch Notes in and Out L/R out.

categories.name: Drum Machines
categories.blurb: Whole kits that play by themselves with the transport: patch Out L/R to the output.

categories.name: Drums/Kicks
categories.blurb: One-shot bass drums, from 808 boom to distorted gabber: patch a trigger into Trig.

categories.name: Drums/Snares & Claps
categories.blurb: One-shot snares and handclaps for the backbeat: patch a trigger into Trig.

categories.name: Drums/Hats & Cymbals
categories.blurb: Hi-hats with Closed and Open triggers, and crash, ride and splash cymbals.

categories.name: Drums/Toms & Percussion
categories.blurb: Toms, hand drums and small percussion: patch a trigger into Trig.

categories.name: Drums/FX
categories.blurb: Zaps, lasers, metal, bells and noise hits for fills and transitions.

categories.name: Sequencers
categories.blurb: Note sources that follow the transport: patch Notes into any Voice Cell.

categories.name: Effects
categories.blurb: Stereo insert effects: patch In L/R from any sound and take Out L/R onwards.

categories.name: Processors
categories.blurb: Pitch, modulation, dynamics and tone effects: shimmer, doubling, flanging, phasing, sidechain pumping and lo-fi.

categories.name: Modulators
categories.blurb: Control, gate and trigger sources for everything else on the board: LFOs, randomness, envelopes and rhythms.

categories.name: Generative
categories.blurb: Self-playing patches: press play and they make music on their own, in time with the transport. Out L/R out.

categories.name: Starters
categories.blurb: Empty cells to start your own instrument or effect from.

categories.name: Test
categories.blurb: Presets for trying things out by hand in a host.

preset.description: Two saws detuned ±7 cents into a saturating transistor ladder, with a soft filter envelope and slow release.
Square wave and sub octave through a 1-pole low-pass, organ-style on/off envelope and a shared vibrato LFO.
Detuned saw pair from Dual Osc into a ladder whose envelope swells in with the notes: synth brass stabs and swells.
Wavetable Osc on the Digital bank: each note sweeps through the table, a stereo-detuned bright poly. Shared input Position.
Dual Osc as a two-operator FM piano: a sine modulator an octave up whose index decays with each note, harder with velocity.
Chord Osc stacks a minor seventh on every key into a resonant low-pass with a short envelope: dub-techno chord stabs.
Formant Osc whose resonant peak glides up with each note and settles: glassy, vocal keys with stereo spread.
Macro Osc in Phase Warp: each note starts bright and relaxes towards a sine, like a phase-distortion digital keyboard.
Swarm in unison: eight drifting, detuned oscillators per note spread across the stereo field, through a bright low-pass.
Saw through a screaming diode ladder with a snappy filter envelope; harder notes open it further like a 303 accent, and legato notes slide. Shared input Cutoff.
A sine an octave below the key with a whisper of triangle for audibility on small speakers, softly saturated: deep, clean sub bass.
Dual Osc saws detuned 14 cents apart into a ladder whose cutoff drifts on a slow LFO and opens with aftertouch: the rolling drum-and-bass reese. Shared input Cutoff.
Macro Osc in FM mode: a 1:1 modulator whose index snaps down after each attack, with a little feedback grit. Punchy, woody digital bass. Shared input Index.
The Folder's internal sine folded hard on every attack and by aftertouch, rounded off by a ladder: a snarling, West Coast growl bass. Shared input Fold.
Narrow pulse and sub square through a saturating state-variable low-pass with a short, velocity-sensitive pluck: a round funk and house bass.
Wavetable Osc on the FM bank with a sub, through a resonant ladder whose cutoff wobbles in eighth notes with the transport. Shared inputs Cutoff and Table.
Formant Osc an octave down with its resonant peak swept by an envelope and pressure, so each note says "yow": a talking, vocal bass. Shared input Formant.
Dual Osc hard-synced to a core an octave below; an envelope tears the synced core's pitch down on every note, under a driven low-pass. Shared input Sync Sweep.
A slightly FM'd triangle pinged through a Low Pass Gate and held open by the gate: rubbery, bouncy bass that darkens as it fades, no envelope needed.
Two slightly detuned saws into a warm ladder with a vibrato that fades in on held notes; legato notes glide. Shared inputs Cutoff and Bend (±2 semitones).
A slowly swept PWM square whose width and brightness follow aftertouch; the shared Mod input adds vibrato depth, as a mod wheel would. Shared inputs Mod and Cutoff.
Dual Osc in hard sync: an envelope rips the synced core's pitch up and a slow LFO keeps it tearing while held, into a driven filter. Shared input Sync Sweep.
Macro Osc in FM mode at a bell-like ratio, its index bright on the strike and mellowing as the note rings: a chiming bell lead for slow melodies.
The Folder's internal triangle folded more with velocity and aftertouch while a slow LFO bends its symmetry: a glassy-to-gnarly West Coast lead. Shared input Fold.
Macro Osc's sung-vowel model: each note opens from "o" towards "a", with a delayed vibrato and a touch of breath. A wordless solo voice. Shared input Vowel.
A rounded triangle-and-saw blend that slides slowly to every new note, theremin-like with a gentle vibrato: for long, singing portamento lines. Shared input Bend (±12 semitones).
A raw, unfiltered 12.5 % pulse whose width flips with the tempo in sixteenths and a quick delayed vibrato: a game-console chiptune lead.
Swarm in unison: six detuned, drifting saws per note spread wide, through a resonant low-pass with a filter envelope: a buzzing, huge trance lead. Shared input Cutoff.
A soft triangle with pink breath noise band-passed at the note, a slow attack and pressure-controlled breathiness: an airy, flute-like lead. Shared input Breath.
Two saws a few cents apart, each voice drifting at its own rate, into a soft ladder that swells open: a lush analog string pad. Shared input Cutoff.
Ten Swarm oscillators bloom from unison into stacked fifths while Organic LFOs breathe on spread, warp and filter: a wide, living cloud. Shared input Bloom.
Additive Osc with a chorus on its partials and a comb that sweeps slowly through them, differently per voice: an airy organ-choir. Shared input Air.
Wavetable Osc on the Spectra bank, scanned along a spiral by a slow tide LFO and offset per voice, through a gentle ladder. Shared input Scan.
Macro Osc's Vowel model: each voice drifts through its own vowels with a slow vibrato fading in, a little breath on top: a formant choir. Shared input Vowel.
Two pulse waves whose widths sweep in opposite phase, at a slightly different speed per voice, into a warm ladder: a shimmering PWM pad. Shared input Cutoff.
Dual Osc saw over a triangle an octave down, lightly folded, into a low resonant ladder that Organic LFOs open and close over many seconds: a dark drone. Shared input Cutoff.
Modal Voice bows an inharmonic glass body that swells in after a soft mallet ting; a slow LFO wanders the bow position and aftertouch bows harder. Shared input Brightness.
Chord Osc spreads an open major seventh over the stereo field with a chorus-like detune, through a phaser that sweeps slowly: an ensemble pad for one-finger chords. Shared input Cutoff.
Pink noise through a pair of resonant band-passes tuned to the note, gusting and turning as Organic LFOs move them: a pitched wind texture. Shared input Howl (resonance).
Modal Voice strikes a wooden bar: soft felt mallets that harden and brighten with velocity, a warm, short ring. Shared input Brightness.
Modal Voice strikes long-ringing metal bars, with a motor tremolo on the amp: a mellow vibraphone; velocity hardens the mallet. Shared input Tremolo Rate.
Resonator's String model plucked near the end on every note, odd and even partials split left and right; velocity plucks brighter and the strings ring on after release. Shared input Brightness.
Macro Osc's plucked string picked hard near the bridge, starting a shade sharp and settling, with a vibrato that fades in on held notes: a koto-like pluck.
Perc Voice strikes metal tines (bar partials) with a soft click and a short, woody ring; velocity is the accent and every voice is struck a little differently.
Perc Voice's FM engine between membrane and bar ratios, a bright attack that mellows into a hollow ring: a steel drum; harder hits are brighter.
Macro Osc's two-operator FM at an inharmonic 3.5 ratio, struck by each note with a long decay that darkens as it fades; velocity raises the index. Shared input Index.
A lightly folded, FM'd Dual Osc pinged through a resonant Low Pass Gate whose light also opens the folder: the woody West-coast bongo. Shared inputs Brightness and Decay.
Macro Osc's Modal model an octave up, hard and bright with slightly stretched modes: the plinking comb of a music box; velocity is the strike.
A short noise burst, louder and brighter with velocity, hammers a stiff metal string in the Resonator: a ringing hammered dulcimer. Shared input Brightness.
Drum Map plays a Ring kick, snare, clap and hats; move the shared X and Y inputs to travel between grooves, hold Fill for fills.
A Gate Sequencer with probabilities and ratchets plays Macro Osc's Kick, Snare and Metal models and a Perc Voice FM blip. Shared input Fill.
Rhythm Bank's four related even rhythms play a skin, a wood block, a bar and a shaker from Perc Voices, in a small room. Shared input Pattern browses grooves.
Drum Grid electro: syncopated Punch kick, snare and clap on the backbeat, busy hats, cowbell and a zapping tom; two patterns.
Minimal techno on a Drum Grid: a dry Punch kick, off-beat Ring hats and a syncopated rim sent into a tempo-synced dub echo and a dark room.
A two-bar breakbeat (kick, ghosted snare, ride) through Bender, which repeats, reverses and reshuffles slices by chance. Shared inputs Chaos and Glitch.
Lo-fi boom-bap: a lazy swung Ring kit through a saturated ladder low-pass and a light bit crush, over a bed of tape hiss.
Rotating Div turns the 16th-note clock into /2 … /7 cycles on kick, hats, conga, clave, cowbell and clap: polyrhythms that realign every four bars. Shared input Rotate.
A long, round 808-style boom: a low sine with a gentle pitch drop and a hint of drive.
A short, punchy 909-style kick with a fast sweep and a clicky attack.
A hard, driven kick through a saturating ladder filter: thick, warehouse-ready.
A very low, long kick that dives into the sub range, low-passed to pure weight.
A short, bright click kick on top of a rounder body kick: punch and weight together.
The Macro Osc kick model, darkened and crunched by a driven ladder filter.
A modal drum head tuned low: an acoustic-leaning kick with a soft beater click.
A fully driven kick, wavefolded and low-passed: the distorted hardcore thump.
A warm, mid-length kick, rolled off above 2.5 kHz for deep house and dub.
An FM kick: a low carrier with a fast-falling index for a rubbery, electronic thud.
A classic 808-style snare: two tuned heads and a short burst of noise.
A bright, snappy 909-style snare with plenty of rattle.
A low, long snare with a quiet clap underneath for width and body.
A snappy snare into a big, damped room: an arena backbeat.
The Macro Osc snare model: a synthetic snare with a tight, papery body.
A noise-bank snare: a cloud of filtered noise with a sharp click and almost no tone.
An 808-style handclap: four quick noise bursts and a short tail.
A brighter, tighter 909-style handclap.
Two differently tuned claps panned hard left and right: a wide, crowd-like clap.
A clap in a small, live room.
808-style hi-hats from six square waves: Closed and Open, and Closed cuts the open hat.
Crisp 909-style hi-hats with a little crunch: Closed and Open, and Closed cuts the open hat.
Very short, bright hats high-passed at 7 kHz: ticks for fast patterns.
Detuned, fully crunched hats with a long, washy open hat.
Hats from two noise-bank voices, high-passed; Closed chokes the open hat.
Hats from the Macro Osc metal model: clangy, ring-modulated and inharmonic.
A bright crash cymbal with a three-second wash.
A ride cymbal: a defined ping over a long, quiet shimmer.
An 808-style cymbal: square-wave metal with a long, hissy decay.
A small, high, short crash for accents.
A deep 808-style tom with a soft pitch bend; retune it for high, mid and low toms.
A punchy 909-style mid tom with a strong pitch bend.
An FM syn-tom with a steep downward sweep: the classic electronic pew.
A low, long floor tom in a small room.
A modal conga: a warm, slightly bending skin with a palm slap.
An 808-style cowbell: two detuned square waves through a band-pass.
A short, woody clave click.
A sharp, short rimshot.
A short burst of high noise-bank grains, high-passed: a shaker for 16ths.
Jingles from a bright open hat over a quiet, low clave for the skin.
A short FM zap: a high pitch that falls to nothing in 150 ms.
A longer, brighter FM sweep into a wide space: a sci-fi laser shot.
The Macro Osc metal model, ringing for most of a second: a clangy industrial hit.
A struck modal bell an octave up, into a hall.
A metallic modal bar with a rimshot strike: a hard, ringing anvil.
A short burst of dust, wavefolded and band-passed: digital crackle for glitchy fills.
A rim click rings a bank of modal resonators: a tuned, wide, glassy hit.
A deep, driven boom with a crash on top, into a big hall: a transition hit.
A falling noise-bank whoosh into a long space: a downlifter on every hit.
A tiny, pure FM blip: a short tonal tick for percussive melodies.
A 16-step A Phrygian acid line with ties for slides and loud accents: play a mono Voice Cell with Legato and Glide. Shared inputs Transpose and Reset.
A two-bar E minor bassline bouncing between octaves, moving to C in the second bar: disco and house bass. Shared input Transpose follows a key change or a chord sequencer.
Harmony Master plays Am7 – Fmaj7 – Cmaj7 – G7, two bars each, as sustained chords (and the chord root on Root) on harmony Bus D. Shared inputs Transpose and Reset.
A D Dorian progression (Dm – G – Dm – C) from Harmony Master on Bus D, arpeggiated by Quantizer Suite as seventh chords over two octaves, up and down in 16ths.
A Turing-machine melody: an 8-bit Shift Register that mutates now and then, quantized to E minor pentatonic over two octaves. Shared inputs Lock (frozen ↔ random) and Transpose.
Polymeter Seq in F Dorian: rhythm 16, notes 5, octaves 7, gates 12 and chances 9 steps long, so the line keeps turning over for hundreds of bars. Shared input Transpose.
Stage Seq in C harmonic minor: eight stages of held notes, repeats, a ratchet and two slides make a one-bar riff with a four-bar phrase. Shared inputs Transpose and Hold.
Cartesian Seq in F Lydian walks a 4 × 3 grid of bright broken chords: a twelve-step figure that shifts against the bar; Mod rises through the grid. Shared input Transpose.
A random melodic walk: Random steps on each 8th, quantized to D Dorian, with a looping coin deciding which 8ths play. Shared inputs Loop (new ↔ repeating) and Transpose.
Recall draws random 16th-note gates and A minor pentatonic notes that keep echoing their recent past: half new, half remembered. Shared inputs Memory (more = repeats) and Reset.
A gentle high-pass keeps the lows out of a big, dark hall with 40 ms pre-delay and a six-second tail. Shared inputs Mix and Freeze.
Tempo-synced dotted-eighth echoes that bounce left and right, darker with every pass, into a short room. Shared inputs Feedback and Tone.
Grains pitched up an octave with octave-and-fifth jitter feed back into a long reverb: a shimmering halo above anything. Shared inputs Mix and Freeze.
A short tape-style delay whose head drifts with wow, flutter and a slow LFO: warm chorus and seasick tape wobble. Shared input Depth.
A resonant tanh ladder swept up and down by a triangle locked to half notes: a tempo auto-filter for pads, chords and loops. Shared inputs Cutoff and Depth.
A frequency shifter with tight feedback: phaser notches that rise forever, turning in opposite directions in the two ears. Shared input Speed.
Bender catches sixteenth-note slices by chance and repeats, reverses and re-pitches them in octaves: seeded glitches that come back every loop. Shared inputs Chance and Glitch.
A touch of wavefolding, constant sample-rate and bit crushing and a dull low-pass: a worn, crunchy sampler sound. Shared input Grit.
Ten narrow band-passes tuned to C minor pentatonic, a slow window scanning across them: drums and noise turn into ringing, tuned chords. Shared input Scan.
A VCA chopped on sixteenths by a synced square with softened edges: rhythmic trance gate for pads and drones. Shared input Depth.

The reverb's tail is pitched up an octave and fed back into it, so every echo climbs: a halo of ever higher voices above the sound. A limiter keeps the loop bounded. Shared inputs Mix, Shimmer (loop amount) and Freeze.
The same loop, but a fifth up: each echo moves to the next fifth, so the halo is open and suspended rather than bright. A longer window keeps it smooth. Shared inputs Mix, Shimmer and Freeze.
A copy of the sound an octave down, with its top taken off, mixed under the original: a bass, a lead or a kick gets a floor. Shared input Sub (the amount of the lower octave).
Two copies, a few cents sharp and flat, each wandering a little, plus a light chorus: a single voice or lead becomes a small ensemble. Shared input Spread (the detune).
A short, resonant flanger on a slow sweep: the whoosh of a jet passing over drums, noise or a full mix. Shared inputs Rate and Feedback.
Eight allpass stages sweeping slowly and wide, the right ear half a cycle behind the left: notches that travel through a pad, strings or an electric piano. Shared inputs Speed and Feedback.

Patch a kick or any rhythmic sound into Sidechain and the sound on In L/R is pushed down with every hit, then swells back: the pumping of dance music. Shared inputs Sidechain, Depth (lowers the threshold) and Release.
Five bits, a quarter of the sample rate, a drive and a band-limiting EQ: music through a failing radio or a 90s sampler. Shared input Damage.
Everything below 500 Hz and above 3 kHz removed, a bump in the middle and a touch of drive: a voice or a drum loop down the line. Shared input Drive.

The speed errors of a worn tape machine: a slow wow and a quick flutter wobble the pitch by a few cents, with a darker top, a little saturation and drift. Shared inputs Wow and Flutter (the depth of each).
Four tempo-locked LFOs from one Quad LFO, at a quarter, a half, one and two bars: sines and triangles that always meet on the downbeat. Shared input Hold.
Four slow organic LFOs that wander like a living group, plus their sum: subtle analog drift for cutoffs, pans and detune. Shared input Speed.
One random stream on quarter notes in three shapes: stepped sample-and-hold, a smooth walk and a springy wobble, plus burst triggers. Shared input Clock.
A Tidal slope looping every two bars with a slow rise and quick fall, in four phase-shifted copies for staggered swells. Shared inputs Restart and Skew.
A two-bar breathing loop that never stops, and a six-second exponential swell each time Trigger fires: slow movement for pads and drones.
Six-way randomness from Uncertainty: two slow fluctuating curves, eighth-note quantized steps in fifths and a bell-shaped value stored every half note. Shared input Clock.
Two leaky neurons that fire and inhibit each other: a steady gate, an irregular one, their XOR and A's charging ramp. Shared input Excite speeds them up.
A six-stage Segments envelope on the Gate input: a snap up, a dip, a slow bloom to a held sustain, then a two-stage fall. Shared input Stretch scales every time.
Sixteenth and eighth clocks through weighted coins that repeat every 16 tosses: two probabilistic gate streams and the accents where both land. Shared input Chance.
Macro movement locked to the bars: a smoothed rise over four bars, an up-and-down arc over the same four, and a pulse at the start of each phrase.
Random gates tossed between three pinged low pass gates, each tuned to a fresh D minor pentatonic note: a west-coast hand-drum garden that keeps shifting. Shared input Density.
A Shift Register melody in A Dorian plucks a string Resonator while a sine bass echoes the same bits four steps later, through a dotted-eighth delay network. Shared input Lock (frozen ↔ mutating).
Four soft voices of a D♭ major-seven chord, each swelling on its own free-running loop of 18 to 29 seconds so they never line up the same way twice, into a wobbling tape delay and a long hall.
Gusts of chance triggers strike two bell-like Modal Voices tuned to F major pentatonic, slow organic movement on where they are struck, in a wide reverb. Shared input Wind (more strikes).

A generative techno loop: Drum Map kick, clap and hats with a touch of chaos, and a Polymeter Seq acid line in A minor through a resonant diode ladder whose cutoff drifts like weather. Shared input Cutoff.

A Harmony Master (bus D) walks a repeating loop of four D minor seventh chords, two bars each: a saw pad holds the chord tones, a plucked bass follows the chord's bass note, and a Pluck arpeggio traces the chord. Shared input Root (transposes everything).

A twelve-voice Swarm on a C minor ninth, breathing through a scale-tuned Filter Bank; eight related Organic LFOs slowly move its spread, cross-FM and the bank's scan and shift. Shared input Root (pitch).
Four Modal Voice marimba bars on C minor-seventh chord tones, struck every 2, 3, 5 and 7 sixteenths; a slow random rotates which bar gets which prime, so the polyrhythm turns over every four bars.
Sparse Lydian plucks from a Macro Osc feed Grains, which scatters them back at wandering positions, an octave or a fifth away, with feedback and blur: a slowly shimmering cloud. Shared input Density.

Two Neurons firing at each other, nudged by slow organic drift, play metallic FM clicks, a modal knock, noise ticks and a rim; Bender glitches the mix and a scattered delay smears it. Shared input Excite (fires faster).
A blank Voice Cell: notes in, nothing inside yet. Open the board and patch your own voice between Voice In and Voice Out.
A blank effect: the audio passes straight through. Open the board and put your own modules between In and Out.
A pentatonic melody that plays with the transport, through Verb (medium room). Move Size, Decay and Mix while it plays; Mix at 100 % leaves only the tail.
